beats.narration_text: Hi, I'm Sai Pranavi J. This video is about an API filter that rejected the exact labels our own classifier generates, a one-line type fix that closes a gap I flagged, but didn't fix, in last week's report.
beats.new_visual_element: Personal-intro card: fellow's name + one-line summary of what the video covers, spoken

shot.note: Same pattern as this fellow's other episodes' B01.

beats.narration_text: Our source classifier doesn't just pick from a short list anymore. For Federal Register items outside the big three regulators, it builds the label on the fly. Our filter endpoint never got the memo.
beats.new_visual_element: A short list of 5 fixed labels next to a sixth, dynamically-built label, visually flagged as the odd one out

shot.note: Real framing of the fixed-enum vs dynamic-label mismatch, not illustrative.

beats.narration_text: Here's the real enum, straight from the models file. Five fixed source labels. But the real classifier, identifySource, builds a sixth kind of label on the fly: Federal Register, dash, whatever agency actually issued it. Department of Labor, Department of Education, any agency that isn't SEC, CFTC, or FINRA. That label was never in the enum, and never could be.
beats.new_visual_element: The real 5-value SourceFeed enum shown verbatim, next to the real identifySource() template string that builds the dynamic label

shot.note: [Source: models.py, workflow.dev.json identifySource()] Verbatim enum values and template string, not paraphrased.

beats.narration_text: The filter endpoint typed that parameter as the fixed enum. Any dynamic label failed validation before my own code ever ran, a 422, not a filter. The fix is two lines: widen the type to a plain string, and stop calling dot-value on an enum that's no longer there. The database column was always just a string underneath.
beats.new_visual_element: The real two-line diff from commit 565e84e, both the import line and the parameter/pass-through line

shot.note: [Source: feeds.py commit 565e84e] Real diff, matches the committed fix exactly.

beats.narration_text: Before trusting the fix, I mounted the real router behind a FastAPI test client, with the database layer mocked out, and sent the same dynamic label through both versions. The old signature: four twenty two, enum validation error, exact label rejected. The new signature: two hundred, and the mocked database function received the real string, unchanged. A known fixed label still passed cleanly both times, no regression.
beats.new_visual_element: The real before/after table from this session's live TestClient run (422 -> 200), with the fixed-label row shown as unchanged in both

shot.note: [Source: verification/verify_source_feed_output.txt] Real measured TestClient results from this session, not illustrative.

beats.narration_text: Two honest limits. First: nothing shows this 422 ever hit a real user, the frontend doesn't currently send this parameter at all, so this closes a latent gap, not an observed incident. Second: this verification mocked the database layer. It confirms the API layer now accepts and forwards the real label correctly, it doesn't confirm a live query against a database that actually contains rows with these dynamic labels.
beats.new_visual_element: 2 honest-limit cards, side by side, full weight, no softening language

shot.note: [Source: FACTCHECK.md #6, #7] Full weight, not softened, per established house discipline.

beats.narration_text: When a classifier is allowed to get smarter, every consumer of its output has to be allowed to keep up, including the one-line type signature nobody thinks to revisit.
